newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan sees no need to slow economy.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan sees no need to slow economy.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said parts of the economy were growing at a rapid pace, but that overall there was no need to slow growth to ease pressure on trade accounts.
"At the moment, we see no need for restrictive measures. There are sectors of the economy showing great expansion, like durable goods, but others are not," Malan told a seminar on banking.
Some economists have argued for the past several months that Brasilia will come under increasing pressure to block rising imports by adopting stiffer credit restrictions.
They say the country's burgeoning trade gap -- which hit $5.5 billion in 1996 and is expected to growth to $8.0 billion this year -- is simply putting too much pressure on the current account.

Malan refused to comment on February's trade data, which is due out tomorrow. He added, however, that the January and February trade balance, expected to be $2.0 billion in the red, was not representative of the year as a whole.
"The result based on the first two months has no significance," he said.
